record.original_question: For a preemptive uniprocessor real-time system modeled as a finite sporadic task system tau = {tau_1, ..., tau_n}, where each task tau_i has worst-case execution time C_i, relative deadline D_i, and period T_i, generates jobs at least T_i time units apart, and each generated job requires at most C_i execution and has deadline D_i time units after its arrival, determine the computational complexity of deciding fixed-priority schedulability in the implicit-deadline case D_i = T_i for every task. The input includes a specified total priority order on the tasks, and fixed-priority scheduling always executes an incomplete job of the highest-priority task. Is tau schedulable under that specified priority order, meaning that all deadlines are met for every legal sequence of job arrivals?

evidence.quote: A sporadic task τiis characterized by three parameters — a worst-case execution time Ci, a relative deadline Di, and a period Ti.
For a given scheduling algorithm A, τ is said to be A-schedulable if algorithm A meets all deadlines when scheduling every collection of job arrivals that may legally be generated by τ .

Problem 1 (Computational complexity of FP schedulability analysis – implicit deadline tasks.) What is the computational complexity of the following problem? Input: Implicit-deadline sporadic task system τ, with a specified priority assignment on (a total ordering of) the tasks in τ. Question: Is τ FP-schedulable with the specified priority assignment?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a preemptive uniprocessor real-time system modeled as a finite sporadic task system τ = {τ₁, …, τₙ}. Each task τᵢ is described by three positive parameters: a worst-case execution time Cᵢ, a relative deadline Dᵢ, and a period Tᵢ. Task τᵢ may generate an infinite sequence of jobs, subject to the constraint that consecutive jobs of τᵢ are released at least Tᵢ time units apart; each released job requires at most Cᵢ units of processor execution and must complete within Dᵢ time units after its release. A scheduling algorithm A is said to schedule τ successfully if, for every legal sequence of job releases that τ may generate, A meets every job's deadline. Fixed-priority (FP) scheduling is the algorithm that, given a total priority order on the tasks, at each instant executes some incomplete job belonging to the highest-priority task that currently has an unfinished released job.

Restrict attention to implicit-deadline task systems, i.e., systems in which Dᵢ = Tᵢ for every i. The decision problem FP-SCHED(implicit) is: given as input an implicit-deadline sporadic task system τ together with a specified total priority ordering on its tasks (with all parameters encoded in binary), decide whether τ is FP-schedulable under the given priority ordering.

Determine the exact computational complexity of FP-SCHED(implicit). In particular, is it decidable in polynomial time, is it NP-hard or coNP-hard, or does it lie at some intermediate level of complexity?
artifact.status_search_result: The exact computational complexity of fixed-priority schedulability for implicit-deadline sporadic task systems remains a recognized open problem, but partial results exist. Notably, it has been shown that rate-monotonic schedulability of implicit-deadline tasks becomes NP-hard once the utilization is allowed to exceed the Liu–Layland bound ln 2, while the Liu–Layland test gives a polynomial-time sufficient condition below that bound. A complete classification (e.g., in P vs. NP-complete vs. coNP-complete) for arbitrary priority orderings does not appear to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Rate-Monotonic Schedulability of Implicit-Deadline Tasks is NP-hard Beyond Liu and Layland's Bound
status_evidence.snippet: FP-schedulability problem is NP-complete even if restricted to task sets with RM priorities and utilization bounded from above by any constant c > ln(2).
status_evidence.claim: Partial hardness result: NP-hardness holds for RM priority above the Liu-Layland bound, but exact complexity of general FP-schedulability for implicit-deadline tasks is not fully settled.
